body:
We should add `--use-router` option, so instead of directly attaching claude/codex files to tasks' docker, we pass `--use-router` option, that will access specific hive-mind-router docker on the docker network.

We also need to make sure https://github.com/link-assistant/router actually supports sync with global claude/codex files/folders, so it is possible to mount claude/codex files and folders from root hive mind docker container to it, and it will be the only point of contact with AI subscription.

When working with hive-mind-router docker, our telegram bot must ensure we only keep hive-mind-router container running, when there any task that uses it. For each separate task we should have separate token issued, so each task will have its own separate logs.

When task is about to get finished, we should take claude/codex sessions data from it, and merge it to hive-mind-router container or root hive-mind container, as that may be needed for security audit, we also need to mount a folder for router data folder, so all logs are preserved, and can be used for audit of any issues or security checks.

By default we keep current mechanics of direct mount of claude/codex mount, but when `--use-router` is enabled, we isolate each task from directly accessing claude/codex subscriptions.

That feature should be marked experimental, it should also support formal-ai routing when used with `--model formal-ai`, so everything goes through the same router/proxy.

We should also configure each task's gh and git tools to use router, and we should immediately apply block of all delete operations or history changes like git reset and so on detected up on git push, or used directly via gh API. That way we limit physical ability to destroy any data by our AI agents by default.

We need to make sure we will be able to access logs of task/router and so on if needed, so we should also double check everything in that scope. So if anything will go wrong it will be an easy to collect the data and fix it. We should have special docs section about collecting logs though out of the system, not just for router, so for next issues everything will be simplified.

If https://github.com/link-assistant/router has missing features for anything described, we should first report issues there, once they are fully implemented we can continue delivering results on this task here in this repository's pull request.

We need to collect data related about the issue to this repository, make sure we compile that data to `./docs/case-studies/issue-{id}` folder, and use it to do deep case study analysis (also make sure to search online for additional facts and data), list of each and all requirements from the issue, and propose possible solutions and solution plans for each requirement (we should also check known existing components/libraries, that solve similar problem or can help in solutions).
title: `--use-router` option
